state.intent:
- A review round that returns only refinement — wording, numbers, naming, softer claims — still gets answered with a fix commit *and* another round, and the next round returns refinement again. PR #238 ran six fix rounds after its full review; the last two returned nothing but refinement, and each cost a round.
- Nothing written says when a loop ends, so the owner had to say it by hand: 리뷰 루프에서 결함 없이 refining 만 남는다면 그거 적용까지만 하고 종료하는 것을 원칙으로 하자.
state.plan:
| step | change |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | `reviewing.md` § The shape of a round: one sentence — a round returning only refinement is applied in one commit, reviewed narrowed on that diff, and merged; no further round is commissioned. Carries the #238 measurement. |
| 2 | `AGENTS.md` § The fix round: the same rule in one sentence, no measurement, pointing at the reference as the section already does. |

- Constraint: prose only. No script, no test, no guard — the rule is a judgement about a review's *content* and no checker can read it.
- Constraint: `AGENTS.md` is also touched by #237. This is two sentences in one section; a conflict there is a hand resolution, not a redesign.

state.intent: - The scenario–test–code tie is a rule a machine can decide, and today nothing decides it: a commit that adds code with no scenario, or a scenario no test names, passes every guard.
state.plan:
- Waits on the model sub-issue's merge; the tie and the skip rule are read from `spec/sdlc`, and the check's docstring cites them.
- Read `check-tree-shape.py` for the shape of a refusing guard here, and `feedback-guard-tests` in the memory pool for how a refusal is tested.
- Start with the narrowest decidable tie — a scenario name appearing in a test name and a test name in the code path's test — and widen only when a named case demands it.
- Constraint: the check reads names, never verdicts; a solver verdict stays the solver's.

- Two follow-ups #246 left for the next sub-issue touching `scripts/` (NOTE on #246): widen `check-cross-references.py` `ABSOLUTE_PREFIXES` from `spec/campaign/` to `spec/`, with a case in its suite; teach `alloy-check.py --digest` the sdlc signatures (`LETTER`) and relations (`VARYING`), so an sdlc trace digests to more than its events.

state.definition_of_done:
- `scripts/check-merge-review.py <pr>` reads the pull request's head sha and its comments, and refuses when no comment opening `REVIEW` names that sha; it prints the head, every `REVIEW` sha it read, and which branch it took; an unreadable pull request is `could not look`, not a pass.
- The same script, given a `REPORT` comment body, refuses one whose sha is not the head.
- Its suite has one named failing case per refusal branch, pr#262's shape among them, each failing when its branch is deleted.
- `campaign-claim.py release` calls it before deleting a merged claim's ref and refuses on its verdict; `.github/workflows/check.yml` runs it as a required status on the pull request head, so a merge without a `REVIEW` at that sha is refused by GitHub.
- `AGENTS.md` § Merge conditions replaces "read by nothing" with the mechanism's name.
…
state.intent:
- Merge condition 1 — a review read at the sha being merged — has no reader: pr#262 merged at 8ca2609 with zero comments opening `REVIEW` and zero pull-request reviews (NOTE on sdlc-alloy#247, 2026-09-09), and nothing refused it. `AGENTS.md` § Merge conditions says as much: "condition 1 is readable and read by nothing".
- A `REPORT` that pins a sha other than the head is the same gap from the other side: the review it asks for is at a sha nobody will merge.
- Reopened 2026-09-10: a posted `REVIEW` fires no workflow, so every merge waits on a hand `gh run rerun` (baseline#1 friction list).
state.plan:
- Read `check-campaign-claim.py`'s `COMMENT_CEILING` block for how a `REVIEW` first line is parsed today; reuse it, do not restate it.
- Script and suite first; then the `release` hook; then CI; then the prose. One commit each so reviews narrow.
- Constraint: the script reads GitHub through `gh`, never a pane or a transcript.

- `spec/campaign/session/system.als` or `orchestration/system.als` models a fleet-wide instruction: one owner word, delivered to every listed session of the named role, with the hand-off it demands (successor launched on the named model, state handed over, the old session leaving by `leave`).
- One script reads `herdr agent list`, filters by role and, where asked, by the model read from each transcript, and prompts each matching pane with the instruction; it prints what it read, whom it addressed, whom it skipped and why.
- The prompt names `planner.md` § Handing off (already written, model `handoff`), never restates it; `launching.md`'s model table no longer pins the planner to Fable.
- A merged pull request lands all of it, reviewed at its sha; `check-rule-readers` passes.
state.intent:
- The owner's order of 2026-09-14 ("every planner on Fable hands off to an Opus high planner", rule-check#245 comment 5659188284) moved by hand: one peer read every transcript, one message per planner.
- Nothing in `spec/campaign/` names one instruction addressed to every session of a role at once, and no script delivers one: `campaign-assign.py` and `herdr agent prompt` address one pane each.
- The owner asked (same comment) that the scenario be specified or built into the harness, so one short instruction moves every planner.
state.plan:
- Run `scripts/campaign-context.py <this issue>` first; read the owner comment and `planner.md` § The planner's clock.
- Step 1, the spec: add the scenario, strictly simpler on the three counted measures (a field before a new sig).
- Step 2, the script, `--dry-run` first (lists targets, prompts nothing). Model read from the transcript's last assistant `model`; no transcript reads `unknown` and is skipped.
- Step 3: the model table in `launching.md`, one line, and the reference the prompt cites.
- Pull request on the first commit; the worker runs its own review (Opus high) and posts REVIEW at the sha.
